THE JOB RECORD / A PRACTICAL GUIDE

Choosing a simple job tracker for handyman work

A simple job tracker should keep visits, time and costs together. FieldSoli is a free option for independent contractors and handymen who also want estimates and invoices, without a required subscription.

FieldSoli · November 2026 · 4-minute read

IN THIS GUIDE

01 — Job basics02 — Visits and time03 — Materials and costs04 — Notes and changes05 — Payment status06 — A simple example07 — Using FieldSoli

What to check before choosing a job tracker

Try a job that takes two visits. Check whether you can add time afterward, record materials and other expenses, and find the original notes again. Then check whether estimates and invoices stay with that same job.

FieldSoli supports those records, searchable job history and CSV job-summary export without an active subscription. Add jobs from marketplaces or your own customers manually; there is no automatic marketplace import. If you need crew dispatch, routing or accounting, those fall outside FieldSoli’s current scope.

Start with the job basics.

Give each job a clear name. “Drywall patch and paint — hallway” is more useful to search later than “Tuesday job.” Add the customer’s name, contact details and the address where the work takes place.

Record the agreed work in plain language. Include the room, fixture or repair involved and anything excluded from the scope. If the job came through Angi, Thumbtack or a referral, note that source in your records. It is separate from the work itself.

Keep a record of each visit.

A job may take several visits. Keep each visit under the same job rather than creating a new job every time you return.

  • Date: when you were there.
  • Time: the hours spent on that visit.
  • Work: a short note about what you completed.
  • Next visit: what still needs to be done, if anything.

Use consistent descriptions for preparation, work on site and other time you choose to record. A saved total is more useful when you can understand what it covers.

Record materials and other costs.

For each material, record a recognizable item name, quantity and cost. Keep materials tied to the job where they were used. Record other job costs, such as parking, separately so they are easy to identify.

If your record includes both a purchase cost and an amount charged to the customer, label them clearly. They are not the same figure. For supplies used across multiple jobs, note how much belongs to this job rather than copying the full purchase into every record.

Note changes while they are clear.

Use a short note for a change in scope, a customer request, a material substitution or something that needs a return visit. Include the date and what changed.

A useful note is specific: “Customer requested paint on the full hallway wall; patch-only scope changed.” A note that says only “extra work” leaves too much to reconstruct later.

Keep payment status separate.

Completed work and received payment are different things. Record whether the work is finished and whether payment has been received. An estimate records the proposed work and expected charge. An invoice requests payment for the listed work. Keep each document’s reference with the job record; neither document alone confirms that payment was received.

Update payment status from an actual payment record, not an assumption that a completed job has been paid. This guide covers keeping job details organized, not bookkeeping or tax requirements.

For a closer look at the documents, read estimate, invoice and payment status.

A simple job record.

WORKED EXAMPLE / FICTIONAL JOB

Job: Drywall patch and paint — hallway
Customer: Jordan Lee
Visit 1: 1 hour · patch and preparation
Visit 2: 2 hours · sanding and paint
Total time: 3 hours
Customer charge: $300
Materials: $40
Other recorded costs: $10
Payment status: Unpaid

A simple calculation: $300 − $40 − $10 = $250 remaining before taxes, other overhead and the value of your own time. Dividing $250 by 3 hours gives about $83.33 per recorded hour.

This is before tax and business overhead, not take-home pay. The $300 is still unpaid, and unrecorded time or costs would change the result.

The record does not need to be long. It needs enough detail to show what happened, what was used and what remains open.

Keeping these records in FieldSoli.

FieldSoli is a job tracking app for contractors and handymen. You manually enter job details and keep visits, time, materials, other costs, notes and payment status together. Searchable job history lets you return to those records. Invoices and estimates keep documents with the work. Review recorded job earnings in the earnings summary.

Jobs from Angi, Thumbtack and referrals can be entered manually. FieldSoli does not automatically import or sync with those services.

DOCUMENTS & PAYMENTS / A PRACTICAL GUIDE

Free contractor invoices and estimates: what to check

FieldSoli offers free unlimited invoices and estimates with no required subscription. Check document limits, sharing and payment tracking before choosing an invoicing app.

FieldSoli · November 2026 · 3-minute read

IN THIS GUIDE

01 — The proposed work02 — The payment request03 — The money received04 — A quick review05 — Using FieldSoli

Check what free includes

Look beyond the download price: check how many estimates and invoices you can create and whether sharing or export requires a paid subscription. FieldSoli has no monthly invoice or estimate limit. You can create and share them alongside your job records without a paid subscription.

You can also request a CSV job summary without an active subscription. This is job-summary data, not a complete account backup. Current free access does not promise every future feature will be free.

Check how invoices fit your work

If you track visits, time, materials and expenses separately, consider whether keeping estimates and invoices with the job would simplify your records. FieldSoli keeps those records together. It records payment status but does not process payments from customers.

Start with the estimate.

An estimate describes the work you expect to do and the expected charge. Make the description specific enough to recognize the job: the location, task and items included. Note any assumptions that could change the amount, such as the materials needed or the extent of a repair.

Keep the estimate reference with the job. If the proposed work changes, record the revised scope and amount rather than relying on memory. An estimate is not a record of completed work or money received.

Check the invoice against the work.

An invoice lists the work or items you are requesting payment for. Before sharing it, check the customer details, job description, quantities and amounts. Compare it with the agreed scope and your notes about any changes.

Keep a clear reference so you can match the invoice to the right job later. If you revise a document, distinguish it from the earlier copy. Avoid treating both copies as separate amounts owed. Creating or sending the invoice is a document step, not proof of payment.

Update payment status from a payment record.

Check what actually arrived before marking a job paid. Note the amount, date and reference in your records so a later review does not depend on remembering a conversation.

If only part of the requested amount arrives, keep that distinction clear. For example, an invoice for $500 with $200 received leaves $300 outstanding, assuming there are no other adjustments. The job may be finished while payment remains incomplete.

Review three separate questions.

  • What was proposed? Check the estimate and any changes to the scope.
  • What was requested? Check the invoice and confirm you are looking at the current document.
  • What was received? Check the actual payment record and identify any amount still outstanding.

These questions help separate a change to the work from a change to the document or a payment still to come. You do not need a long note for each step; you need enough detail to understand why the figures differ.

Keep the documents with the job.

In FieldSoli, create estimates and invoices with customer details and job items, and track payment status alongside the work. Use the visits, costs and notes in the job record as context when reviewing your documents.

For the broader record, including hours and materials, read what to track for each handyman job. This guide is about keeping job information clear, not accounting, legal or tax requirements.

CHOOSING SOFTWARE / A PRACTICAL GUIDE

Can a free app replace paid contractor software?

Yes, if your needs are job tracking, time and expenses, estimates and invoices. FieldSoli covers those everyday tasks for independent contractors and handymen, with unlimited invoices and estimates and no required subscription. A larger field service system may be a better fit when you need scheduling, crew dispatch or payment processing.

FieldSoli · Product selection guide

Compare the everyday tasksWhen a larger tool helpsEvaluating a newer appWhy we’re building this

Compare the tasks you actually need

A monthly price does not tell you whether an app fits your work. Compare what happens on an ordinary job: recording the visits, keeping the costs, preparing an estimate and sending the invoice.

FieldSoli’s core-task coverage
Your taskWhat FieldSoli provides free
Keep a job recordJob details, notes, repeat visits and searchable history.
Track time and costsA visit timer, time added afterward, materials and other expenses.
Prepare estimates and invoicesCreate and share documents with no monthly invoice or estimate limit.
Record whether a job is paidRecorded payment status. Customer payment processing is not included.
Take useful records outCSV job-summary export without an active subscription. This is a summary, not a full account backup.

If those are the tasks you use a paid app for, FieldSoli gives you a free way to do them. Compare this checklist with your own workflow.

See the actual app screens, or read the free invoices and estimates guide for document limits, sharing and payment status.

When a larger tool helps

FieldSoli is a focused option for an independent contractor or handyman keeping their own job records. It can replace a paid tool for the basic tasks above when those are the tasks you need.

If your decision depends on crew dispatch, scheduling, routing, accounting or collecting customer payments, compare products that provide those features. FieldSoli does not currently provide them. It also does not automatically import jobs from Angi, Thumbtack or other marketplaces; add those jobs manually.

Compare the plan you would actually use, not just a product’s free-download label. Check document caps, export access, the features you need and the total ongoing price. Other free products may also suit your work.

How to evaluate an app with few reviews

FieldSoli is new, and public feedback is still building. A small review history gives you less independent evidence about long-term use. Screenshots and feature descriptions help you check fit, but they do not replace your own evaluation or customer reviews.

  1. Create a sample job with realistic details that are safe to use for testing.
  2. Record a visit, time, materials and another expense. Check the saved amounts and job history.
  3. Create an estimate and invoice, inspect the preview, and try sharing to yourself.
  4. Try a CSV job-summary export and inspect what it includes before depending on it for your records.
  5. Check the current store listing’s reviews and updates, and contact support with any questions before moving your regular workflow.
